recipes.name: Old Time Chicken Divan
ingredients_raw: 2 cooked chicken breast halves - bones and skin removed, cut into 1/4 inch slices

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add broccoli, and cook until just tender, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain and rinse well with cold water to chill. Place drained broccoli into a 9x13 inch baking dish and set aside.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour, and cook, whisking constantly, until the flour begins to turn from white, to a pale beige, about 3 minutes. Whisk in sherry, chicken broth, and heavy cream until smooth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 5 minutes; season with salt and pepper.

Pour half of the hot cream sauce over the broccoli and top with chicken slices. Stir Parmesan cheese into the remaining sauce, and pour over the chicken slices. Sprinkle top with extra cheese, if desired.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes or until heated through, then broil for a few minutes until top has turned golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Old Time Chicken Divan
raw_recipe.description: This company-worthy casserole is made with chicken breasts, fresh broccoli, and a sherry cream sauce. Top with sliced almonds, if desired.

review.reviewBody: The real deal and worth the effort. If you note the other reviews, the ones with less than four or five stars all say that they substituted main ingredients (fried chicken?). Do us a favor and don't review if you make major alterations to a dish. Submit a new recipe instead.

While I have to size down when cooking for just two I also try to reduce waste. I steam the broccoli in the chicken stock so I don't have salty water with lots of vitamins to put down the drain. A little smoked paparika adds something to the flavor. I make this or a similar dish about monthly but varying the seasonings. Experiment and enjoy.

DELICIOUS! This is a very easy recipe to make and it is outstanding. Made half of the recipe (for just 2 people) using fresh broccoli and 1 boneless chicken breast that I steamed in my rice cooker while the rice was cooking. Cooked the chicken breast in a pan and then made the sauce in the same pan to add to the flavor of the sauce. Used a 1.5 qt casserole dish to cook. Wow, this is definitely a keeper. Many thanks for this recipe.

This is so good. I use 4 boneless skinless chicken thighs, cooked in a bit of olive oil. I add the butter to the pan I cooked the chicken in, and add the flour to make the roux. I cut the chicken in 1" chunks and place on the broccoli. In the sauce I use homemade bone broth and add a sprinkling of thyme in addition to the sherry. I never have whipping cream, so use half & half. After pouring it over the broccoli and chicken I grate as much parmesan as necessary to make a nice coating. Then bake. Does not really take all that long. So good! Thank you.

I followed the recipe ingredients but changed the cooking method to make this a one pot dish. I cooked a diced chicken breast with sliced fresh mushrooms in olive oil. While this was cooking, I chopped the two heads of broccoli florets and added them to the pan. I also made the sauce in the same pan using butter, flour, chicken broth and 2% milk (I didn't have sherry or cream). I added about a tsp of pepper, 1/8 cup of dried minced onion and 1/2 tsp of minced garlic to the sauce as it cooked. I also added the parmesan cheese to the sauce as it thickened and threw in 1/3 cup of sharp cheddar cheese that I wanted to use up. After baking in the oven, the flavors seemed to meld really well. We liked this a lot but felt like that amount of broccoli was a little overwhelming. I will probably make this again but not on a regular basis. Thank you for the recipe.

UPDATE 1/2024: Yea, a chicken divan recipe with no soups! That's what I said again when I saw this again. ... My review: Made 99% as is, but just par-steamed the broccoli for less cleanup and added a pinch of garlic powder to the sauce. Hands-down the best -- and most authentic -- chicken divan recipe on this site!
Very good! I added breadcrumbs on top - highly recommend! Melt 4 T butter until frothy, add 1 cup fresh bread crumbs. Cook on medium until brown.
Everything was good. I pan fried chicken breasts in avocado oil and herbs de province. Sliced it then finished in the oven by the directions. I was out of cream and used half n half. Cream is best.

What an awesome recipe! I did brown the sliced chicken in olive oil and garlic, swapped the sherry for white cooking wine, added 1/4 tsp curry powder to the sauce, and topped it with sliced almonds. What a beautiful presentation it made and it was soooo delicious! Highly, highly recommend this succulent, creamy delight!

This a great base for this recipe and I really love that it doesn't use canned soup b/c I really hate canned soup. I made changes according to my liking. I used about 5 heads of broccoli (yeah I know its a lot of broccoli) and a 1 1/2 lbs of chicken breast. I had some leftover cooked brown rice and placed that first in a single layer at the bottom of the 9x13 pan. I then placed raw broccoli florets on top of that. I lightly cooked the chicken and placed it on top of the broccoli. I doubled the sauce. For the sauce: 1) I used Better than Bullion chicken base 2) I sauteed a butt load of garlic in butter (5-6 cloves) 3) I used about a cup of Cabernet Sauvignon b/c I didn't have any sherry or white wine. This made the dish delicious but it also made the sauce come out a not-so-appealing color. 4) I kept the amount of heavy cream at 1/2 cup 5) I kept the amount of Parmesan cheese at 1/4 cup but added 3 thick slices of muenster cheese b/c this is all the cheese I had on hand.
I cooked it at 350 for about an hour. It was great.

This was a tasty dish and not complex to prepare. I made very minor changes which are as follows:
To the melted butter, before adding flour, I added a few cloves of minced garlic and sauteed slightly.
I did not have cream on hand and substituted whole milk- and it turned out fine.
I did not have black pepper but sprinkled in some white pepper instead. 
Other than that, I followed the recipe as written, only doubling the sauce. I made it with leftover turkey and served over pasta. Creamy, rich, and delicious!
Great. Made according to recipe. Used chicken from Simple Baked Chicken Breasts from this site. Added almonds as suggested above.

This is delicious....and it repeats beautifully as well. You could use any cream of soup, I did chicken w herbs. This would also be good w cauliflower instead of broccoli. I added French fried onions on top.
As a “casserole” don’t think too much. It seems to be more of a topping but not sure to what. However, in and of itself, it is quite tasty. Just strange as a stand-alone recipe.
I love that it's the way my mother and grandmother would make it: from scratch with no frozen products and no canned soup!
So glad to find a good recipe without soup or mayonnaise. this is the real classic delicious recipe
My husband’s favorite meal!

My friends and family love this recipe. I did change it up a bit. Used asparagus instead of broccoli. I also add sauteed sliced mushrooms and 1 package of thick broad noodles and double the sauce. Also top with cheese and Ritz crackers,

This is my go-to Chicken Divan recipe, made many times over the years. Although the use of cream and sherry may appear to be a bit over the top, they are the perfection you're looking for. So don't change a thing -- it's perfect as it is! Okay, I'll allow you to increase the amount of parmesan cheese. Enjoy!

Made pretty much as written. Only had white wine so did substitute that. Ok. Very plain. Maybe don’t like chicken divan. Probably will use leftover chicken in something other than this dish next time.
